Alex Chen: Quick sync — we need to lock Q3 roadmap decisions for the deployables workstream (VPC control plane, on‑prem packaging, air‑gap). Customer pilots asking for dates. Can we triage scope today?
Marta Rios: +1. Two customers pushed for on‑prem pilot in H2, want SLA + audit logs. Are we treating control plane and packaging as separate deliverables?
Vikram Singh: They have to be coupled for most enterprise flows but we can phase deliverables: (1) VPC control plane (lightweight API for tenant mgmt + auth), (2) on‑prem packaging (installer + runtime), (3) full air‑gap support (offline package + attestation).
Jess Liu: From QA perspective we need clear acceptance criteria per phase. Suggest a minimal checklist for customer pilot: 1) deploy from our installer, 2) register cluster to control plane, 3) model serving end‑to‑end with sample workload, 4) audit logs to KMS.
Ryan O'Neil: Also need SLA expectations and rollback story. For pilots we should say "best effort" but with clear telemetry. Legal wants a list of supported topologies for pilot contracts.
Alex Chen: Proposed priority: A) control plane API + auth (enables many customers), B) packaging MVP (single node + kube manifests), C) air‑gap baseline (staged). Thoughts?
Marta Rios: I worry if we leave air‑gap too late — compliance customers will walk. Could we scope air‑gap MVP as "downloadable artifacts + install guidance" (no attestation) in parallel with packaging?
Vikram Singh: Technically feasible to create an artifacts bundle early, but attestation & signing/verification is a separate engineering chunk. We can split:
```
- artifacts bundle (tar + checksums)
- install CLI (offline installer)
- signing/attestation (HSM/KMS integration)
```
Doable in parallel if we staff a small sprint team.
Jess Liu: Test matrix grows if we parallelize. We need one integration lane for pilot customers to avoid fragmentation.
Alex Chen: OK tradeoff. Proposal: ship artifacts bundle + docs in MVP1 (parallel), but block customer GA on signing/attestation (MVP2). That gives sales something to demo.
Ryan O'Neil: Agree. For launch criteria (pilot->GA) recommend these must be met:
- Resilience: 99.9% model serving baseline under pilot load
- Security: RBAC + audit logs to customer KMS
- Observability: per-route latency + token cost breakdown
- Installability: <2 hour unattended install for single‑node
Additions?
Marta Rios: Add: documented recovery steps and upgrade path must be tested.
Vikram Singh: Add: a rollback path for runtime image and control plane schema changes.
Alex Chen: Good. I'll draft a short "Launch criteria" doc and link in threads. Action items: Alex to draft, Marta to vet legal/contract language, Vikram to estimate eng effort, Jess to draft QA matrix, Ryan to write pilot SLA blurb. Dates?
Marta Rios: Can you target draft by EOD Friday? Legal needs two business days after that.
Vikram Singh: I'll do rough estimates by Monday. If we get a small dedicated eng pod we can parallelize artifacts + control plane in 6 weeks for pilot MVP.
Jess Liu: QA matrix by next Wed. Will include 3 sample load profiles and integration checklist.
Ryan O'Neil: I'll draft pilot SLA + supported topology list by Monday.
ops-bot: Link to backlog epic: https://redwood.internal/epics/DEPL-4372 — current blocks: packaging-nightly fails on debian-12 image, control-plane auth token rotation missing.
Alex Chen: Noted. Blockers are actionable — Vikram can you own debian-12 fix?
Vikram Singh: Yeah I'll pick it up. Expect PR by Tue.
Marta Rios: We're missing a clear ask from the earliest pilot customer (FinBank). I'll ping their SE to get required compliance checklist tomorrow.
Alex Chen: Cool. Decision recap: control plane prioritized first to enable registration + telemetry; artifacts bundle shipped early for demos; attestation/signing deferred to MVP2; launch criteria agreed (resilience, security, observability, installability, recovery/rollback). Owners & dates assigned.
Jess Liu: :thumbsup:
Ryan O'Neil: +1, will loop in sales for pilot expectation alignment.
Marta Rios: Will update contract template once Alex posts draft.
Alex Chen: Thanks team. I'll post the draft criteria here shortly and create the follow‑up ticket with the action items.
